sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) Public relations is a ______ communication process. (ii) The main aim of PR is to build ______.
State true or false: (a) The Chief editor oversees PR. (b) A Photo Division gives official photographs to the media.
Match: (i) Product PR (ii) Employee relations (iii) Community relations (iv) Political relations with (a) newsletters (b) window display (c) public libraries (d) rallies and posters.
Fill in the blanks: The key public of hospitals are ______, of schools ______, of television ______.
State true or false: (i) Systematic practice of PR in India began with the Indian Railways in the 1920s. (ii) PR is a sender-controlled phenomenon.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: List any three purposes of Public Relations.
questions.answer: To educate audiences on the advantages of a product; to promote goodwill for the organisation; to create, maintain and protect the organisation's reputation.

questions.q: List any four media units under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
questions.answer: AIR, Doordarshan Kendra, Films Division, Press Information Bureau (also DAVP, Photo Division).

questions.q: Describe the functions of PIB and DAVP.
questions.answer: PIB issues official press releases to the media; DAVP handles publicity campaigns and advertising for central ministries.

questions.q: Define public relations.
questions.answer: A form of communication used to persuade or influence people by ethical means through two-way communication between an organisation and its public.

questions.q: What is the role of the Song and Drama Division?
questions.answer: It uses music, drama and folk media to publicise government programmes through performing artists.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Define public relations and explain its importance.
questions.answer: PR is a two-way ethical communication to persuade the public; it builds goodwill, educates about products and policies, creates and protects reputation and wins public support.

questions.q: Describe the functions of any two government media units that help in communicating policies to the public.
questions.answer: PIB issues press releases to print media; DAVP releases advertisements and runs publicity campaigns; Song and Drama Division uses folk media.

questions.q: Explain product PR and employee relations.
questions.answer: Product PR launches products through samples, events, exhibitions and window display; employee relations earn goodwill through newsletters, bulletin boards, picnics and incentives.

questions.q: Explain community relations with examples.
questions.answer: Organisations gain community goodwill through parks, clean-up drives, charitable dispensaries, sponsorships, public libraries and fund-raising in calamities.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe the structure of government public relations in India.
questions.answer: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (information, broadcasting, film) has media units such as AIR, DDK, PIB, DAVP, Films Division, Photo Division and Song and Drama Division; states have Directorates of Information and Public Relations.

questions.q: Explain the types of public relations.
questions.answer: Product PR, employee relations, government and political relations and community relations, each with its methods.
